The runtime integration extends the existing [PostHog telemetry path](/internal/docs/posthog). It adds standard OpenTelemetry context for supported tool dispatches, application child spans, outgoing Node HTTP/fetch calls and inference-gateway model observations. Existing invocation, workflow, testing and acceptance records remain the evidence authority.

Implementation is under verification in the staging tree. This document does not attest shipment.

## Composition and correlation

Host bootstrap initializes the process provider before DBOS boot. `PROJECTED_DEPS.onDispatchStart` starts a tool span; `aroundInvoke` binds its context during the handler; `recordInvocation` ends it and adds `metadata_json.otel` with traceId, spanId and traceFlags. This OTel identity is separate from the existing MCP request UUID. An inbound valid W3C traceparent supplies parentage. Baggage is neither accepted nor propagated.

The maintained HTTP and Undici instrumentations create outgoing spans only when a tracked parent exists. Standard application tracers inherit stable invocation attributes. The gateway extracts traceparent at request start and ends its model span through the existing request-stage completion callback, including failure/cancellation outcomes. DBOS uses the already registered provider through its supported tracingEnabled configuration. This does not establish that every detached workflow, every CLI model request or every remote service participates in a common trace.

## Consent and data vocabulary

Export uses the existing host/key/install-id resolver and requires production plus telemetry opt-in or the explicit internal-build authority. Hosted customer tool dispatches are excluded from this exporter; the separate customer diagnostics authority remains separate. The opt-in timestamp prevents queued observations from an earlier consent grant being sent after revocation and a later grant.

Only finite scalar allowlisted fields leave the process: stable runtime references, outcome/error code, model/provider identity and available token/timing counters. Raw span names, arbitrary attributes, exception messages/stacks, prompts, responses, tool arguments, request URLs and headers are excluded. Model output tokens are not currently supplied by the gateway timeline; missing observations are not represented as zero. Exporter network requests suppress tracing to avoid a capture feedback loop.

## Delivery and health

PostHog receives ai_trace/ai_span/ai_generation events (with their standard dollar-prefixed names), and sanitized exception observations. Stable per-span event UUIDs support ingestion deduplication. The batch processor uses at most 2048 outstanding observations and batches of at most64; delivery has a2s network timeout and the SDK a3s export timeout. Active request state is capped at1024; abandoned entries are expired when the next request begins after30min.

`dev:telemetry.observability` reports process-local health. tracing.active is the active request-map size; skipped counts duplicate IDs or active-cap rejection; expired counts reclaimed request entries; queuedSpans includes queued and in-flight export observations; queueDroppedSpans counts observations refused at that cap. posthog.exportedSpans counts spans accepted by the capture HTTP endpoint, not query-verified storage; failedSpans counts failed exporter deliveries; consentDroppedSpans counts excluded observations. These counters reset on process restart and do not constitute an audit ledger.

## Verification

Run the repository test router for packages/operator-core/lib/observability/tracing.test.ts, posthog-exporter.test.ts and runtime.integration.test.ts. The integration fixture invokes the real production dispatch hooks and configuration resolver, uses an isolated HTTP model/capture receiver, and verifies outgoing context, sanitized events, invocation metadata and revoked-consent behavior. The consent epoch regression lives in endpoint-route/routes/desktop/setup-wizard-state.test.ts.

Before live acceptance, select the maintained current-build route with dev:pipeline_position using testClass operator-api and verify which build is loaded. Final shipment additionally needs the exact green release artifact and a synthetic trace read back from the configured PostHog project. Capture HTTP acceptance alone is not that readback.
